I'm working through layer 0 head by head, starting with how far each head's attention pattern diverges from uniform, measured as KL. Next I'm comparing each head's actual output against what it would produce with uniform attention, and I'm checking how large that error is relative to the residual stream.

I'm now comparing the dropped-head error against the replacement error and then choosing the head whose uniform replacement changes the output least.

import numpy as np, json
A=np.load('pass_23/attention_L1.npy').astype(np.float64); H0=np.load('pass_23/token_hidden_L0.npy').astype(np.float64)
H1b=np.load('pass_23/token_hidden_L1.npy'); msk=np.load('pass_23/attention_mask.npy').astype(bool)
P='bert.encoder.layer.0.attention.'
Wv=W(P+'self.value.weight').astype(np.float64); bv=W(P+'self.value.bias').astype(np.float64)
Wo=W(P+'output.dense.weight').astype(np.float64); bo=W(P+'output.dense.bias').astype(np.float64)
V=H0@Wv.T+bv  # n,T,768
n,T,_=H0.shape
tot=np.zeros((n,T,768)); outs=[]
for h in range(12):
    sl=slice(64*h,64*h+64)
    ctx=np.einsum('nts,nsd->ntd',A[:,h],V[:,:,sl])
    o=ctx@Wo[:,sl].T; outs.append(o); tot+=o
tot+=bo
U=H0+tot  # pre-LN
den=np.sqrt(((U[msk]-U[msk].mean(1,keepdims=True))**2).sum(1)).mean()
L=msk.sum(1)
for h in range(12):
    sl=slice(64*h,64*h+64)
    mV=(V[:,:,sl]*msk[:,:,None]).sum(1)/L[:,None]  # uniform mean
    ou=np.repeat((mV@Wo[:,sl].T)[:,None,:],T,1)
    err_unif=np.linalg.norm((outs[h]-ou)[msk],axis=1).mean()/den
    err_drop=np.linalg.norm(outs[h][msk],axis=1).mean()/den
    # entropy ratio
    a=A[:,h]; ent=-(a*np.log(a+1e-12)).sum(-1); entu=np.log(L)[:,None]
    er=(ent/entu)[msk].mean()
    print(h,'unif-replace err %.4f  drop err %.4f  entropy/uniform %.3f'%(err_unif,err_drop,er))
